 JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner is as follows:-
That on 06-09-2023 at about 7-20 pm., the petitioner was riding a Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05- LP-9633 on 1st main road, Jayanagar 8th Block, Bangalore,
at that time the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-17-7978 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner motorcycle, result of which the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately, petitioner was shifted to Sevakshetra Hospital wherein first aid treatment was given and then he was shifted to NIMHANS Hospital.
Thereafter, the petitioner has taken conservative treatment at Dayananda Hospital.
So far, the petitioner has spent more than Rs.1,00,000/- towards medical expenses and other incidental charges.
3. Prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy.
He has aged about 29 years.
He was doing street Vegetable Seller and earning sum of Rs.40,000/-.
Due to the accidental injuries, petitioner has suffered pain and sufferings, permanent disability, loss of future income and other pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.
4. Respondent No.1/

the insurer of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-17-7978 has filed written statement and admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.

The respondent No.1 has contended that the driver of the insured vehicle was not holding a valid driving license and said vehicle was not having FC and that there is delay of 10 days lodging the complaint, that the alleged accident has occurred due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner himself.
The petition is bad for non joinder of necessary and proper parties.
5. Respondent No.2/

the RC owner of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-17-7978 has filed written statement and contended that the said car was insured with the 1 st respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident and submitted that on the date of accident he was driving his vehicle on the extreme left side on the 1st main road, Jayanagar 8th block, Bangalore slowly and cautiously by observing traffic rules and regulations, at that time the petitioner came on his motorcycle on the said road in a rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, without observing any of the traffic rules and regulation and dashed against his vehicle.
Hence, submitted to dismiss the claim petition.

6. Heard the arguments and perused the entire materials placed on record.
7.

Based on the pleadings, this tribunal framed the following:

sentences.text: ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, on 06-09-2023 at about 7-20 pm., on 1st main road, Jayanagara 8th Block, Bangalore City, he sustained grievous injuries due to rash and negligent act of driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-17-N-7978 ?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for Compensation? If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3. What order or Award ?
8.
The petitioner got examined himself as Pw1 and got marked 10 documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P10.

On the other hand, respondent no.2 got examined himself as RW.1 and got marked document as Ex.R1 to Ex.R3.
9.

My findings on the above Issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.

P.W.1 further deposed about the nature of injuries sustained,
treatment taken and the amount spent for treatment etc.
11.

In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving, the P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to 7 which are the police records such as F.I.R with complaint, Spot mahazar, spot sketch,
Notice u/Sec. 133 of IMV Act, reply given thereon, wound certificate, IMV report, charge sheet, etc.,
12.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by the petitioner , case has been registered against the driver of offending vehicle in Crime No.0351/2023 by Jayanagar Police Station for the offence punishable under section 279, 337 of IPC and u/Sec.134(a&b) of MV Act.

After completion of investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable under section 1279, 337 of IPC and u/Sec.134(a&b) r/w 187 of MV Act.
13.

So far as the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is concerned, in the written statement filed by the respondent no.2, he has admitted the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident but denied his rash and negligent driving.

But in the evidence, the respondent no.2 has Anil Kumar .C vs National Ins Co Ltd on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121241808/
3 contended that on the stated date by putting indicator when he was taking right turn at that time he heard big sound.

sentences.text: On his seeing, the rider of one motorcycle was fell on the road.
By parking his vehicle he went to the place where the rider of the motorcycle was lying.
As motorcyclist did not sustain any injuries, he left the place.

By giving evidence to the aforesaid effect, the respondent no.2 has contended that his vehicle was not involved in the accident and his vehicle has not touched to the motorcycle and that since it was raining, the rider of the motorcycle by riding his vehicle in a rash and negligent manner fell down due to skid.
14.

If the contention taken by the respondent no.2 in his written statement and in his evidence is,
compared with the version taken is contradictory in nature.

As observed supra, in the written statement the respondent no.2 has admitted the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident and stated that the motorcycle itself has dashed to his vehicle but not his vehicle dashed to the motorcycle.
Whereas in the evidence the respondent no.2 has disputed the very involvement of offending vehicle in the accident and deposed that the motorcyclist fell down from the vehicle due to skid.
Hence, the evidence of respondent no.2 is not reliable one.
The court has to consider the averments of the written statement.
15. It is true that there is delay of 10 days in lodging the complaint as accident in question has occurred on 06-09-2023 and complaint came to be lodged on 16-09-2023.
In the complaint lodged by the brother of the petitioner he has stated that since petitioner was taking treatment in the hospital they could not lodge the complaint.

But if the medical records and the averments of the petition and the evidence of PW.1 is perused, the petitioner at first has taken treatment at Sevakshetra Hospital and thereafter at NIMHANS Hospital.
In the said two hospitals he has not taken treatment as inpatient and only conservative treatment was given.
As per the wound certificate and as per the averments of the petition, the petitioner has sustained only abrasion injury on his face.
Hence, the petitioner could have lodged the complaint soon after the accident.
Further the petitioner has not produced MLC to prove that the treatment taken by him was towards the injuries sustained in the Road Traffic Accident.

But considering the written statement filed by the respondent no.2 wherein he has admitted the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident, it can be said that even though there is delay of 10 days in lodging the complaint and though MLC was not registered but the petitioner has sustained injuries due to the accident.
16. If the spot mahazar and sketch is perused, at the time of accident the petitioner was proceeding in 1 st main road, 8th Block Jayanagar in 40th cross road.
The offending vehicle which came from same direction took right turn towards 42nd cross road and hit to the motorcycle of the petitioner while taking right turn.
The respondent no.2 in his evidence has stated that since his vehicle was not involved in the accident, no damage was caused to his vehicle.
17. If the IMV report is perused, the vehicle was subjected to inspection by the RTO on 20-09-2023.
It is after lapse of nearly 14 days from the date of accident the offending vehicle was subject to inspection.
Hence, in the long duration of 14 days there is every possibility of respondent no.2 get his vehicle repaired.
Further as observed supra, the respondent no.2 himself in his written statement has stated that the motorcycle has hit to his vehicle.
If that being the case some amount of damage would have been caused to the offending vehicle.

Hence, merely because no damage was Anil Kumar .C vs National Ins Co Ltd on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121241808/
4 found on the offending vehicle at the time of IMV inspection it cannot be said that offending vehicle was not involved in the accident.

sentences.text: Hence, considering the averments of the written statement and the evidence of PW.1 coupled with police documents it can be said that the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is the cause for the accident.
Hence, issue no.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
18. Issue No.2:- The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of his sustained grievous injuries.
As observed earlier, petitioner has produced medical documents i.e., Wound certificate which are marked at Ex.P5.
On going through the medical document it reveals that petitioner has taken treatment at National Institute of Mental Health and Neuro Sciences, Bangalore.

entities.text: National Institute of Mental Health and Neuro Sciences, Bangalore
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: As per wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained one injury which is simple in nature.

19. It is submitted by the petitioner that he was street vegetable seller and earning sum of Rs.40,000/- per month and due to the accident it could not possible for him to do the said work and that on account of the injuries sustained by him he is getting pain every now and then which incapacitated him from doing the work as before the accident.
20. Now coming to the aspect of quantifying the compensation on different heads, the petitioner has suffered one simply injury which made him to suffer pain and agony.
The petitioner has produced medical bills for Rs.4,356/-.
As observed supra, the petitioner has sustained only abrasion injury on his face.
He has not taken treatment as inpatient.
Only on 06-09-2023 he had taken treatment both at Sevakshetra Hospital and NIMHANS Hospital.
But the petitioner contends that on 13-06-2023 he had taken treatment at Dayananda Sagar Hospital.

If the medical bills issued from Dayananda Sagar Hospital dated 13-09-2023, 11- 11-2023 is perused, the petitioner has purchased nutrition supplements used to treat Vitim C deficiency, skin infection, acid related problem and anxiety disorder.
Hence, it can be said that what ever the medicine he has purchased on 13-09-2023 and 11-11- 2023 is not related to the injuries sustained in the accident.
Further the petitioner has produced cash bill dated 10-11-2023 for x-ray taken for cervical spine.
The petitioner has not sustained injuries in the accident on cervical spine so as to take x-ray.
Hence, cash bill dated 10-11-2023 for an amount of Rs.450/- cannot be considered.

Further the petitioner has produced bill dated 16-2-2024 for abdomen and pelvis test for Rs.1000/- and tax Invoice dated 16-05-2024 for the purchase of mobizox tablet at Rs.236/- and Cash bill dated 06-05-2024 issued from V.S.
Dental College and Hospital for TMJ Limitation view for Rs.170/-.
21.

When petitioner has sustained only abrasion injury and taken treatment only for one day that too as outpatient, there is no reason to believe that all the aforesaid medicine purchased by the petitioner are towards the injuries sustained in the accident.

Hence, out of the medical bills produced by the petitioner, bill cum receipt dated 06-09-2023 for Rs.1000/-, cash receipt dated 06-09-2023 for Rs.350/- and bill dated 06-09-2023 for Rs.348/- is taken into consideration and thus it can be said that petitioner has incurred medical expenses only to the tune of Rs.1,698/-.
22.
The petitioner has not examined the medical officer to prove that he has suffered any disability so as to get compensation under the head loss of future income.

Hence having regard to the pain and agony endured and loss of comforts and amenities on account of sustaining such injuries and as incidental expenses and medical expenses incurred by the petitioner, this Tribunal inclines to award Anil Kumar .C vs National Ins Co Ltd on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121241808/
5 global compensation of Rs.30,000/-.
23.

sentences.text: As regarding liability is concerned, there is no dispute that the offending vehicle was insured with 1st respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further the driver of the offending vehicle had driving license to driver the offending vehicle.
Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question were valid and in force as on the date of accident.

Hence by fastening liability on the respondent no.1, this court directs the respondent no.1 to pay compensation to the petitioner along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount.
Accordingly, Issue No. 2 is answered.
24. Issue No.3:
In the light of the findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.30,000/- (Rupees Thirty Thousand only)
with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The interest for the period from 18-12- 2024 till 11-08-2025 is waived off.
Only for the remaining period the respondent no.1 is liable to pay the interest on the awarded amount in view of the order dated 26-06- 2025.
The Respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation and is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within two months from the date of award.
On deposit entire amount and interest is ordered to be released in favour of the petitioner on proper identification.
Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer directly on computer, corrected and then pronounced by me in open court, on this the 1st day of April 2026.)
(ROOPASHRI) XXII Addl.
SCJ & ACJM Bengaluru.
